**Data.** EU-ForDAM (`value1`, 2000–2022, 16 countries, 77 NUTS units) and the NUTS forest appendix (area and growing stock of spruce, pine, fir, oak, all conifers, all broadleaves). Reported damage only, no gap-filling. 0 = recorded, no damage; missing = left out.

**Units.** Borers = m³ of trees killed; defoliators = ha defoliated (not necessarily killed). The two are never added together.

**Guild vs species.** Guild graphs add up all codes of the guild (aggregate codes included). Species graphs show individual species only. Borers and defoliators are always shown on separate graphs.

**Host tree.** The host tree in the data file; insects feeding on several trees get the wider group (e.g. *L. monacha* spruce and pine, *L. dispar* broadleaves, *Melolontha* all forest). Larch, birch, elm and poplar are not separate in the forest appendix, so those species are divided by all conifers / all broadleaves. Check: damage never exceeds the host in any region and year (except Vienna, where the appendix gives 0 spruce but small spruce bark-beetle damage is reported).

## Things to keep in mind

- Germany carries 52% of all borer damage and Poland 50% of all defoliation; most countries start reporting in 2003 (Austria 2002, Poland 2003, Finland 2012).
- Some dips come from how values were recorded, not from the insects: Bavaria *I. typographus* 2007 (6,000 m³) and 2009 (3,633 m³) next to millions in other years, and 0 in 2015; Hesse and Saxony-Anhalt report 0 for every insect from 2006–2007 on. These are listed in `outputs/tables/CHECK_suspicious_values_for_data_providers.csv`.
- Defoliated hectares are hectare-years: the same stand can count in several years and under several species.
- Averages hide outbreaks: e.g. *L. dispar* averages about 105,000 ha a year but a typical year is about 29,000 ha.
- In the defoliator guild share graphs *Melolontha* is left out (it feeds in all forest, not only broadleaves); it is included in the total-damage graphs.
- Bulgaria and Lithuania single-species growing stocks in the forest appendix are read as 1,000 m³ (otherwise far below their reported damage).
